images.title: One icon for 5 items
images.purpose: Show a scale at work: one icon stands for 5 items, so 2, 4 and 7 icons show 10 pens, 20 pencils and 35 erasers.
images.composition: A title and an icon box at the top, and three rows of icons, one different icon for each of pens, pencils and erasers, with the number of items written at the end of each row.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Title Stationery shop centred at (728, 60) in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (44 px). ICON BOX: a white rounded rectangle (corner radius 16, dark #2B2B2B outline 4 px) x 1010 to 1400, y 100 to 180, holding the text 1 icon = 5 items centred at (1205, 140), dark #1F2937 bold (40 px). THREE ROWS, centred on y 290, 470 and 650, split by two thin construction grey #6B7280 lines (3 px) from x 60 to x 1396 at y 380 and y 560. The row names Pens, Pencils and Erasers are left-aligned at x 80 (dark #1F2937 bold, 40 px). Every icon is flat, teal #0072B2 with a thin dark outline (3 px) and white details, fits a 90 by 90 px cell, and the cells of a row are 110 px apart starting at x 330 (cell k at x 330 + 110 k to 420 + 110 k, k from 0). Row 1, Pens: exactly 2 pen icons (a pen standing upright with a cap, a white clip and a small dark nib), cells x 330 to 420 and 440 to 530. Row 2, Pencils: exactly 4 pencil icons (a pencil drawn on a slant at 45 degrees, with a white sharpened tip, a dark point and a white band at the top end), cells x 330 to 420, 440 to 530, 550 to 640 and 660 to 750. Row 3, Erasers: exactly 7 eraser icons (a horizontal rounded rectangle 84 by 44 px with a white band across one end), cells x 330 to 420, 440 to 530, 550 to 640, 660 to 750, 770 to 860, 880 to 970 and 990 to 1080. At the end of each row, 30 px after its last icon, the number of items written in dark #1F2937 bold (56 px) and centred on the row: 10 after the pens (left edge x 560), 20 after the pencils (left edge x 780) and 35 after the erasers (left edge x 1110). In all there are 13 icons (2 + 4 + 7) in 3 rows, and 1 icon box. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a different number of icons in a row from 2, 4 and 7, or icons of different sizes
a number at the end of a row that is not 10, 20 and 35, or an icon box that does not read 1 icon = 5 items
an icon that is cut off or drawn only in part anywhere
images.takeaway: One icon stands for 5 items: the number of items is the number of icons times 5.
images.description: A pictograph of a stationery shop with 1 icon = 5 items: 2 pen icons for 10 pens, 4 pencil icons for 20 pencils and 7 eraser icons for 35 erasers.
images.context: Concept image for One Icon for Many Items. It follows the idea of the pictograph in your maths book (one icon for every 5 items of each kind, in rows) and uses the numbers of this concept's own example: 10 pens, 20 pencils and 35 erasers.
images.teaching_notes: Let the student count the icons in a row and multiply by 5 before looking at the number at the end. The slip to watch: reading each icon as one item and saying 7 erasers instead of 35.

image_decisions.why: Rows of 2, 4 and 7 icons with the icon box 1 icon = 5 items make the idea of a scale countable, which words alone do not.
